title: Semi-localized ground state in a 1D system with long-range hopping
authors: Murod S. Bahovadinov, Faridun N. Jalolov, Vladimir E. Kravtsov, Boris L. Altshuler, Georgy V. Shlyapnikov
abstract: We study the localization of a quantum particle in a one-dimensional disordered system with long-range hopping amplitudes $t(r)\propto r^{-a}$. In contrast to the standard one-dimensional Anderson model ($a\to\infty$), in which all states are localized and the localization length is minimal at the band edge, the long-range model with $1<a<3/2$ exhibits a disorder-driven transition at the band edge, while high-energy states remain localized at arbitrary disorder strength. We investigate this transition for the ground state in momentum space. In the weak-disorder regime, we derive perturbative expressions for the characteristic functions and moments of the momentum-space wave function, as well as for its fractal dimensions. Our results demonstrate that the ground state exhibits $\it semilocalization$ rather than conventional localization, thereby extending the class of models displaying the unusual $\it semifractality$ of wave functions.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes quantum localization in 1D systems with long-range hopping and disorder. Using advanced perturbation theory and SUSY techniques, the authors find that the ground state exhibits a unique 'semi-localized' state for certain hopping decay rates. This is quantified by a specific set of fractal dimensions, extending the understanding of wave function statistics in disordered quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper investigates the localization properties of a quantum particle in a 1D system subjected to long-range hopping and diagonal disorder, focusing on the ground state in momentum space.
main_result: For specific hopping decay rates ($1 < a < 3/2$), the ground state exhibits 'semi-localization' rather than conventional localization, characterized by a specific set of fractal dimensions $D_q$.
method: The analysis employs weak-disorder perturbation theory in the momentum basis, supplemented by techniques utilizing supersymmetric (SUSY) structure decomposition and asymptotic analysis of wavefunction moments.
model_or_system: The model is a 1D quantum system described by a Hamiltonian with long-range hopping amplitudes $t(r) \propto r^{-a}$ and on-site disorder $\epsilon_i$. The study focuses on the ground state properties.
key_observables: Generalized fractal dimensions ($D_q$), normalized momentum-space intensity ($ho_K$), and the zero-momentum mode weight ($ho_0$).
important_parameters: The hopping decay exponent $a$, which dictates the behavior; the disorder strength $W$; and the hybridization parameter $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on weak-disorder perturbation theory (up to second order in $W$) and asymptotic limits for large system size $L$.
figures_summary: Figures compare Exact Diagonalization (ED) results with Perturbation Theory (PT) predictions for the energy spectrum, moment ratios, and the fractal dimensions $D_q$ across different disorder strengths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the Hamiltonian and the physical problem, applying SUSY and perturbation theory to derive expressions for wavefunction moments, and finally analyzing the asymptotic behavior of these moments to determine the fractal dimensions $D_q$ in different regimes of the parameter $a$.
why_interesting: The concept of 'semi-localization' and the derivation of multifractal spectra provide a detailed theoretical understanding of how disorder affects quantum wavefunctions beyond simple localization/delocalization transitions, which is relevant for understanding transport in disordered quantum materials.
